references.text: The fulfillment of the warning about the hailstorm described as the worst in Egypt's history
Similar language about a plague never seen since the time of the ancestors
The same wording about a disaster without parallel in Egypt's history
The psalmist's retelling of the hail plague that destroyed Egypt's vines and livestock
A poetic description of how God sent hail instead of rain over Egypt
Prophetic use of a hailstorm as an image of God's judgment
Hail as God's instrument of judgment in end-times prophecy
Hail mixed with fire in the Revelation of John, echoing the plagues of Egypt
Enormous hail from heaven as part of God's final judgment
The Lord uses hail as a weapon against Israel's enemies at Gibeon
Jesus uses language from Egypt's unique plagues as a prophetic image of the unsurpassable nature of the final world judgment.
Repetition of the same prophetic allusion to Egypt's unique judgment to describe the final tribulation.
The final judgment in Revelation is presented as an escalation of Egypt's unique plagues, with identical language about unsurpassability.
